Top AI Agent Projects Building on Solana 

AI Agents are growing rapidly on @solana thanks to its high throughput, low fees, and an increasingly mature ecosystem.

In fact, a new generation of AI Agent projects is emerging on Solana, with each project building a different layer of infrastructure for the future of the Agent Economy. 

These are some of the projects currently on my watchlist:

1/ $VVAIFU - @vvaifudotfun 

Often described as the Pumpfun for AI Agents.

A no-code launchpad that allows anyone to create AI agents with their own tokens, manage onchain wallets, and automate activity across X, Discord, and Tg.

At the same time, @clawpumptech has emerged as another major competitor in the AI agent launchpad space on Solana.

2/ SQUIRE - @squire_bot 

An AI agent focused on coding, reviewing pull requests, engaging communities, and supporting developers.

One of the most practical examples of AI utility within the Solana ecosystem.

3/ HYRE - @Hyre_agent 

Building the rails for the agent economy through real-time DeFi intelligence, data streams, inference, and multi-chain identities.

A strong candidate for autonomous trading and personalized DeFi experiences.

4/ @Bloomverse - $AKA

Combining gaming and AI agents, with agents acting as opponents, guides, and dynamic in game participants.

The project sits at the intersection of AI, gaming, NFTs, and virtual worlds.

5/ @cludeproject - $CLUDE

One of the most interesting AI agent projects on Solana today.

Instead of focusing only on conversations or trading, Clude focuses on persistent onchain memory.

Its Proof of Thought model allows important memories and learning history to be permanently committed onchain, creating a tamper-proof record of an agent's evolution.

While many AI projects focus on chatbots and trading bots, $CLUDE is tackling one of the most important challenges for autonomous agents: long term memory and personalization.

title: Ten months later, the $100 Google Home Speaker is finally available for preorder
content: Good things take time, but not all things that take time are good. The jury is still out on the Google Home Speaker, but it certainly took a while to arrive. After announcing its new speaker last August, Google finally has a release date. The company's first new smart home speaker in years will launch on June 25, and you can preorder it today for $100 . The generically named Google Home Speaker is Google's first home audio device in almost six years. The last one was the Nest Audio , which debuted back in September 2020. The new device is small and round—an oblate spheroid, technically. It's covered in a partially recycled fabric available in four colors: hazel, porcelain, jade, and berry (jade and berry are limited to the US). Google says the device produces "360-degree sound" for a uniform listening experience anywhere in a room. Google is into lighting effects again. Credit: Google Previous Google speakers included Assistant-style illuminated lights, but the Google Home Speaker features a light ring around the bottom that glows when the device is listening, "thinking," or responding. title: Hacking the atmosphere: Geoengineering gets a reality check
content: Jim Franke pulls away the cover page of a presentation on the wraparound desk in his office, revealing an illustration of an odd-­looking aircraft with massive wings stretching out from a stubby fuselage. The uncrewed plane is soaring thousands of meters higher than commercial jets fly—so high you can see the curvature of the Earth. It’s precisely the type of aircraft one would need to begin artificially cooling the planet. Those outsize wings would keep the plane and its payload aloft in the stratosphere, about a dozen miles (or 20 kilometers) above the surface, where the air is much thinner—as little as 5% the density near the ground. Once at altitude, the plane would release materials that could, after a few steps of chemistry, reflect sunlight back into space. “If you want to get to 20 kilometers in the near term, this is probably the best bet,” says Franke, a research assistant professor at the University of Chicago. Franke is one of a small but growing cohort of scientists focused on the engineering challenges associated with solar geoengineering, the controversial idea that we could deliberately intervene in the climate system to counteract global warming. The concept came from volcanoes. Massive eruptions in the past have reduced temperatures worldwide by blasting sulfur dioxide and other compounds into the stratosphere, where they convert into sunlight-scattering particles. Hundreds of studies in recent decades have suggested that a human attempt to mimic this mechanism would work quickly and efficiently—at least within the confines of climate models. But these computer simulations are approximations of how the real world works. They gloss over numerous challenges. Like the fact that aircraft capable of carrying the necessary loads to the necessary altitudes don’t exist. content:
Impeccable 3.7 brings linting to design.

Until now it was a skill you asked for help. Now it's a design-system-aware feedback loop that runs while your agent builds, catching slop and design drift before they land.

🪝 Design hooks for Claude, Codex, and Cursor
They run after every UI edit and quietly nudge your agent to fix slop and drift. The output isn't another wall of lint: it separates new findings from already-seen ones, flags clean scans, and asks the agent to use judgment. Fix real issues, leave intentional demos alone, save exceptions to config instead of littering your source.

🎨 Slop detection is now project-aware
Reads your actual design system from DESIGN.md, your typography, palette, radius scale, and tokens, and flags drift from your system, not just generic AI slop:
• this font isn't in your design system
• this color is outside your documented palette
• this radius doesn't match your rounded scale
The same engine powers both the hooks and the CLI, and it's where we're investing next.

🖥️ Live Mode, ready for real projects
Svelte/SvelteKit now preview variants as temporary framework components with live params, then accept cleanly back into your source component. Manual text edits got evidence / apply / discard routes, insertions preserve their anchors, and mapped lists and JSX slots clean up far more reliably.

⚡ Leaner core, sharper detector
Rule-level evals across 3 providers and 4 niches cut guidance with no measurable lift and dropped examples that taught models bad patterns. The company has been in talks with the White House since Friday but has yet to secure an agreement that would allow it to reinstate the offerings. Since Mythos debuted in April , Anthropic has claimed—and warned—that the model has advanced capabilities for not only finding software vulnerabilities to help defenders patch them, but also figuring out ways to exploit them that could be used by bad actors. Anthropic itself noted this double-edged sword in its launch of Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5. “A great deal of advanced usage of AI models is dual use: the same queries that are beneficial in the hands of cybersecurity professionals and biology researchers could be dangerous if available to malicious actors,” the company wrote in a blog post last week. With this in mind, the company initially released a version called Mythos Preview to a select consortium as part of a working group known as Project Glasswing. Mythos 5 was also privately released to this group last week, while Claude Fable 5, which is a Mythos-grade model, was released to the general public with specific blocks on its ability to give responses to questions about biology and cybersecurity. title: Windows 11 KB5094126/KB5093998適用後にOfficeが開けない？Microsoftが不具合を認める
content: Microsoftが配信したWindows 11/10の最新パッチ(KB5094126、KB5093998など)を適用した一部の環境で、Officeアプリがサードパーティ製ソフトから起動できなくなる不具合が報告されています。Microsoftもこの問題を正式に認めており、現在修正に向けて対応中です。 影響を受けるのは「OLE オートメーション」を使うアプリ KB5094126 の既知の不具合として以下のような項目が追加されています。 今回の不具合は、 OLE(Object Linking and Embedding)オートメーションを利用してOfficeを呼び出すアプリ に限定されます。会計ソフトや研究支援ツールなどは、内部からWordやExcelを開いて文書を生成したり編集したりする場合がありますが、その連携部分が動かなくなっている状況です。 具体的には次のようなアプリが影響を受ける可能性があります。 CCH Engagement、Workpaper Manager(会計・税務ソフト) Dentrix、Softdent(歯科向け管理ソフト) Zotero(研究・文献管理ツール) その他、Officeを内部で呼び出す業務アプリ全般 症状としては、Office アプリが起動しない／文書が開かないといった動作が発生し、しかも エラーメッセージが表示されないため原因が分かりにくい点が厄介です。Officeアプリ単体では正常に動作し、あくまで「サードパーティ製アプリ > Office」という連携経路が壊れている点に注意が必要です。 Microsoft の対応状況と暫定回避策 Microsoftはすでに問題を認識しており、今後のWindows Updateで修正を提供する予定です。それまでの間の回避策として、サードパーティアプリ経由ではなくOfficeアプリや文書を直接開く方法が案内されています。また企業環境の場合、管理者が、Microsoft サポートに連絡することで追加の回避策を得られる可能性があるとのことです。 今回の不具合は、WindowsのパッチがOfficeそのものを壊したわけではなく、OLEを使った外部アプリとの連携部分に影響が出ている点がポイントです。会計・医療・研究など、Office連携が業務の中心にある現場では特に影響が大きいため、該当アプリを利用している場合は注意が必要です。

title: Windows 11の「秘密の電源設定」でPCの性能と省電力を調整する方法
content: Windows 11には、通常の設定画面からは見えない「CPUブースト挙動」を細かく調整できる隠しオプションが存在します。 現代のCPUは自動でクロックを引き上げる仕組み(ブースト)を備えており、その挙動はOS側から制御することもできるのです。 今回紹介する 「プロセッサパフォーマンスの向上モード(Processor Performance Boost Mode)」 を有効化すると、WindowsがCPUに対してどれくらい積極的にブーストを要求するかを細かく指定できるようになります。本来OEMや上級ユーザー向けのものですが、レジストリを1箇所変更するだけで一般ユーザーでも利用できるようになります。 レジストリ変更で現れる追加モード Neowin が紹介した手順では、レジストリの Attributes 値を 1から2 に変更することで、電源オプション内に複数のブーストモードが出現します。 具体的な手順は次の通りです。 レジストリエディターを開く Win＋Rで regedit と入力して実行。 該当キーへ移動する HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerSettings\54533251-82be-4824-96c1-47b60b740d00\be337238-0d82-4146-a960-4f3749d470c7 Attributesの値を変更する Attributes を右クリックして 値を「1」から「2」に変更 。 Windowsの電源オプションに新項目が出現 これで 「プロセッサパフォーマンスの向上モード(Processor performance boost mode)」 が表示され、5つのブーストモードを選べるようになる。 不具合が出た場合は元に戻せる 値を 2から1に戻す だけで元の状態に復帰。 電源オプションの「プロセッサの電源管理」の中には、通常は「最小/最大のプロセッサの状態」しか表示されませんが、変更後は「プロセッサパフォーマンスの向上モード」が表示され、以下のような詳細なモードが選択可能になります。 無効(Disabled) ：ブースト関連の挙動を無効化 有効(Enabled) ：標準的なブースト挙動（効率寄り） アグレッシブ(Aggressive) ：より積極的に高クロックを維持 効率的な有効化(Efficient Enabled) ：効率を重視しつつ必要な時だけ性能を追加 効率的なアグレッシブ(Efficient Aggressive) ：効率と性能のバランスを重視 アグレッシブ(保証)(Aggressive At Guaranteed) ：保証クロック以上の性能を積極的に要求 効率的なアグレッシブ(保証)(Efficient Aggressive At Guaranteed) ：効率を保ちながら保証クロック以上を狙う これらはCPUがCPPC(Collaborative Processor Performance Control)に対応している場合に有効で、WindowsがCPUに対してどの程度の性能を求めるかを細かく調整できます。 例えばゲームや重い処理で性能を最大限に発揮したい場合は「アグレッシブ」や「アグレッシブ(保証)」を選択し、バッテリー駆動時間や静音性を重視したい人は「効率的な有効化」や「効率的なアグレッシブ」が向いています。 まとめ：無料でできる軽いチューニングとして有用 この隠し設定は、いわゆるオーバークロックのような危険性はなく、Windows側の制御を調整するだけでCPUの挙動を最適化できるのが魅力です。「もう少し性能が欲しい」「逆に省電力寄りにしたい」といったニーズに応じて、無料で簡単に試せる“軽いチューニング”として覚えておく価値があります。

title: The NO FAKES Act Could Silence Satire, Commentary, And News
content: The NO FAKES Act is supposed to target harmful AI-generated impersonations. But in reality, it will make it easier to suppress commentary, satire, and other lawful speech. That's why EFF has signed a letter urging the Senate Judiciary Committee not to advance the bill in its current form. Take action Tell Congress to Say No to NO FAKES In the letter, EFF joins a coalition of civil society groups in pointing out that the bill would import many of the worst features of the DMCA notice-and-takedown system into an even broader range of online expression. Faced with a “heckler’s veto” over legal speech, platforms will have incentives to remove content first and ask questions later. The bill offers no protection for a platform’s judgment about an often difficult question—whether a particular piece of content is satire, parody, commentary, or news. Any platform that guesses wrong faces penalties of up to $750,000 per work. NO FAKES could also undermine the rights of the people it is supposed to protect. The new federal “likeness” right could be licensed or transferred to others, so individuals will lose control over the use of their own face and voice. That’s not theoretical—workers in the entertainment industry are routinely asked to sign broad contracts about the future use of their likenesses. As the letter notes: A background actor who signs a release on set or an ordinary person who clicks through a platform's terms of service could end up with the right to their own face and voice in someone else's hands, for years, with federal enforcement behind it. EFF and the other signatories urge Congress to examine existing legal remedies and pursue narrowly tailored solutions to genuine harms. The last thing we need is a sweeping new intellectual property right that threatens free expression. In addition to EFF, the letter is signed by the Center for Democracy & Technology, the American Civil Liberties Union, Fight for the Future, Foundation for Individual Rights and Expr

title: AI coding agents taught robots how to install GPUs and cut zip ties
content: What happens when you give AI coding agents a lab full of robotic arms, some compute resources, and a “generous token budget” for teaching the robots various tasks? The agents can apparently figure out a training regimen that teaches the robots to successfully cut zip ties and even insert GPUs into thin sockets on motherboards. That glimpse into how AI can act in a fully autonomous way to automate robot training was made possible by a new agent harness framework—software that wraps around AI models to enable their use of various tools while also providing capabilities such as memory, context, constraint, and feedback loops. That agentic harness, called ENPIRE , was developed by robotics researchers at the Nvidia GEAR (Generalist Embodied Agent Research) lab alongside collaborators from Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh and the University of California, Berkeley. “A part of our NVIDIA GEAR lab now self-improves tirelessly overnight,” wrote Jim Fan, director of AI at NVIDIA, in a LinkedIn post . “We just read the reports in the morning.” Read full article Comments
